messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

- First keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff (100). So all eligible events whose received_time <= 100 are visible.

- Then choose the highest visible revision for each event_id (i.e., for each event_id, there may be multiple revisions; we choose the one with the highest revision number among those visible). Revisions replace earlier.

- Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time (100). So we consider events that occur before or at target_time (100). The historical reconstruction goes in (event_time, event_id) order (i.e., primarily by event_time, secondary by event_id presumably lexicographic). We start with initial_stock 17. We apply these events to compute stock evolution, tracking total historical lost (when demand quantity > stock, the unmet portion is lost, i.e., lost sales). Also we need to track stock_at_target (stock after processing events up to time target_time). Also later we need to compute stock_at_horizon after the future schedule is applied (so after historical reconstruction up to target_time, then we apply the future schedule events (which may have event_time > target_time up to horizon_time). The future schedule is hypothetical scenario, not real.

- The future schedule events (given in the input under future_schedule) will be applied after we have reconstructed historical state up to target_time, starting from that stock. Apply future events in event_time + event_id order (presumably as listed, but we need to adhere to sorting by (event_time, event_id)). We need to compute future_lost: the total quantity of unmet demand in the future schedule (including possibly after some earlier events that occurred after target_time but within the horizon). Also we need first_future_stockout_time, which is the earliest future scenario event_time that has unmet demand (i.e., where demand quantity > stock at that moment causing lost sales). If no unmet demand in future schedule, output -1.

- Also we need stock_at_horizon: final stock after applying all future events up to horizon_time (which is time 130). The horizon_time is given as 130, which is the last event time (there is an event at time 130). So after processing all future events (including the one at 130), we report the final stock.
